Prepare Kernel Inputs from Group-Specific Rasters

Source: R/kernel_prep_by_group.R
kernel_prep_by_group.Rd

Assign each observation to one raster map, then prepare one pooled data object for multiScale_optim. Use this when land cover changes across years but the model estimates shared landscape effects and scales.

Usage

kernel_prep_by_group(
  pts,
  raster_stacks,
  group,
  max_D,
  kernel = c("gaussian", "exp", "expow", "fixed"),
  scale_vars = NULL,
  sigma = NULL,
  shape = NULL,
  bin = TRUE,
  nbins = 256L,
  store_cell_data = TRUE,
  progress = FALSE,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

pts

Projected point locations as an sf or SpatVector object. Point order matches group and the returned covariate rows.

raster_stacks

Named list of SpatRaster maps. Each map has the same extent, grid, CRS, layer names, and class coding. Its name identifies a year or other observation group.

group

Character or factor vector, one value per point, identifying the corresponding name in raster_stacks. Every point uses only its assigned map, including cells affected by changes outside the point's immediate location.

max_D

Maximum extraction radius in the projected map units.

kernel

Kernel weighting function; see kernel_prep.

scale_vars

Optional msr_vars specification. By default, each raster layer becomes a kernel-weighted mean covariate.

sigma

Optional starting scales in map units. Defaults to max_D / 2 for each optimized covariate.

shape

Optional starting shapes for the exponential power kernel. Defaults to 2 for each optimized covariate.

bin

Logical. Build pooled distance bins for kernel covariates. Default: TRUE. All observations use one set of bin definitions.

nbins

Number of distance bins when bin = TRUE; default 256.

store_cell_data

Logical. Retain per-cell values and distances. Default: TRUE. Set FALSE for a lean kernel-only binned object; metrics requiring cell detail retain it regardless.

progress

Logical. Display extraction progress. Default FALSE.

verbose

Logical. Print preparation messages. Default TRUE.

Value

A multiScaleR_data list containing:

kernel_dat

Initial covariate data frame, with one row per point. Columns are centered and divided by their pooled standard deviations. Use this in the starting model.

d_list, raw_cov

Named per-point distance vectors (divided by unit_conv) and raster-value matrices. Both are NULL in lean mode.

binned

Pooled distance-bin summaries for kernel covariates, or NULL when bin = FALSE. Each covariate has finite-value sums and counts by point and distance bin.

raster_group

Named character vector recording the map assigned to each point, in input order.

scl_params

Pooled means and standard deviations used to create kernel_dat; the fitted model replaces these with scaling parameters at the optimized scales.

kernel, sigma, shape

Kernel name, initial scales divided by unit_conv, and optional initial shape values.

min_D, max_D, unit_conv

Lower scale bound, maximum extraction radius, and internal distance scaling factor. These are in map units except the internally scaled sigma.

n_covs, scale_vars

Number of optimized covariates and the validated covariate definitions.

resolution, n_cols

Raster cell size and column count, used to calculate landscape configuration metrics.

cell_data_stored

Whether per-cell values and distances are retained.

Pass the full object to multiScale_optim.

Details

Raster maps must be aligned because landscape configuration metrics use cell adjacency and the resulting model assumes common map units. Group-specific maps may contain different missing cells. For kernel covariates, pooled bins track both finite-cell value sums and counts. The fitted model has common slopes and scales unless its formula explicitly includes group interactions. Choose the response likelihood and any group effect according to the sampling design. A pooled model does not establish that effects are stable across years.

See also

kernel_prep, multiScale_optim

Examples

library(terra)
r1 <- rast(nrows = 20, ncols = 20, xmin = 0, xmax = 200,
           ymin = 0, ymax = 200, crs = "EPSG:26915")
values(r1) <- seq_len(ncell(r1)) / ncell(r1)
names(r1) <- "habitat"
r2 <- r1
r2[seq_len(30)] <- 0
pts <- vect(cbind(c(50, 70, 90, 110, 130, 150),
                  c(60, 90, 120, 140, 100, 70)),
            type = "points", crs = crs(r1))
prep <- kernel_prep_by_group(pts, list(y1 = r1, y2 = r2),
                             group = rep(c("y1", "y2"), 3),
                             max_D = 25, verbose = FALSE)
head(prep$kernel_dat)
#>       habitat
#> 1  1.14516205
#> 2  0.17317085
#> 3 -0.79882036
#> 4 -1.43564218
#> 5 -0.06144772
#> 6  0.97757736
